<reason>A very close, high-quality debate. CON landed the sharper individual rebuttals (the walked-in vs released distinction, the Idaho delisting turn, "consent is purchasable," the "no author" grievance mechanism) and closed memorably. But PRO did the more decisive burden-work: when CON demanded a deliberate release over objection that thrived, PRO answered directly with Idaho, Mexican wolves, Jura/Slovenian lynx, and Scottish sea eagles—and CON only contested Idaho, leaving the others untouched. CON's original thesis (coerced release yields dead wolves) was effectively abandoned; the closing slid to a new, untested claim that surviving populations are "managed down to irrelevance," which Idaho's ~1000 wolves under hunting seasons does not obviously support. PRO's decision rule—what happens when the cheque is refused—was clear, and CON's A1 ("move, redesign, fund the cull") concedes the status quo PRO had already shown has failed for a century. PRO made the final comparison easier to decide; CON's late reframe was clever but arrived too late to be tested.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's [B2.1]-[B2.3] gutting PRO's Germany/France/Yellowstone evidence as recolonisation or park geometry, followed by PRO's [A4.1]-[A4.2] answering the resulting pressure question with Idaho, Mexican wolves, lynx and sea eagles—forcing CON to retreat from "wolves die" to "wolves get suppressed."</best_rebuttal>
